title: Word Search
keyIdea: Try every cell as the start. dfs(i, j, index): out of bounds or wrong letter → false; last letter → true; otherwise mark the cell #, try the 4 neighbours for index + 1, restore the cell, return whether any worked.

approaches.name: DFS + backtracking from every cell
approaches.idea: Mark the current cell # so the path can't reuse it, try down / up / right / left, then put the letter back.
approaches.why: Each of the m·n starts can branch into at most 3 new directions per letter (the 4th is where you came from).

quiz.q: Why mark the cell with # before recursing?
options: So the same path can't use that cell twice (# never matches a letter)
To speed up the bounds check
Other paths may need that cell; the board must be unchanged for them

quiz.q: Why does "ABCB" return false on the example board?
options: The only path would need the same B cell twice
B is not on the board
After the first letter, one of the 4 neighbours is the cell you came from (marked #)
